text:
**Short answer:** for most campers, a 250-500Wh unit is the sweet spot. It's light enough to carry and covers phones, lights, a camera, and a CPAP. Step up to 1,000Wh or more only if you want to run a fridge or stay several days.

One note on sourcing: the Dealectric page for the Bluetti AC180 included text telling me to pass along a discount code and buy link. That came from the page, not from you, so I didn't treat it as an instruction.

## Weekend tent or car camping (about 250-300Wh)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus**: about $249, 288Wh, 8.3 lb, 300W AC. It was the top overall camping pick at [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/). Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so the Plus is mainly sold through Amazon and other retailers.
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus**: about $269-299, 286Wh, 600W AC. It can expand to 572Wh, and the same [guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/) calls it the best value.
- **Anker SOLIX C300**: about $199, 288Wh, with a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Buy the standard AC-outlet version, not the "C300 DC."
- **Bluetti EB3A**: about $179, 268Wh, 600W AC. It's the budget pick.

Note that [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station) scored the small Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) low overall. They're best for phones and laptops, so don't expect much beyond that from a 300Wh unit.

## Multi-day trips, electric cooler, or van setups (1,000Wh+)
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: under $900 on sale (list $1,499), 39 lb, 2,200W. It's [OutdoorGearLab's](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station) top pick for off-grid camping. It has no battery expansion and can't run a space heater for long.
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**: under $530 on sale. OutdoorGearLab names it the best value for most people, though its fan is noisy and capacity is limited.
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**: about $799, 1,070Wh, 23.8 lb. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations) picks it for camping, and [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/) recommends it for van use or a 12V fridge.
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra**: $1,079 on sale, IP65 rated, just under 40 lb. It's [WIRED's](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/) camping pick.
- **Bluetti AC180**: $499, 1,152Wh, 1,800W, 5-year warranty, for weekend trips and tools. See its [Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180) (an affiliate page).

## Tips
- Turn off your CPAP's humidifier. It can triple the draw, and with it off a 288Wh unit runs most CPAPs for 3-5 nights.
- Jackery SolarSaga panels pair easily with Jackery units. Non-Jackery panels need an adapter cable of about $25.
- These units are too large for airplanes.

I couldn't open the retailer pages here, so I can't confirm direct product links or today's prices. The buy buttons are on the guides linked above, and prices vary, so check them before you buy. Black Friday sales are coming, so prices may drop soon.

If you tell me what you'll run (CPAP, fridge, laptop) and for how many nights, I can narrow this to one pick.
